title-proc.eng: Consultancy Services to prepare a Strategic Assessment and Preliminary Business Case in relation to the provision of Irish-language based early-years (Naíonra) facilities in Dún Gar

description-proc.eng: Naíonra Garbháin was established in 1981 as an early-immersion Irish-language based educational setting for pre-school children in Dún Garbhán and the surrounding areas. Dún Garbhán is a Baile Seirbhíse Gaeltachta (Gaeltacht Service Town). Naíonra Garbháin provides education and childcare services for people from the Gaeltacht who do not have access to housing in An Rinn or An Sean Phobal and who live in the surrounding area. Naíonra Garbháin is managed by a voluntary committee known as Croí na nÓg. As it is located immediately adjacent to the Irish-language based primary school, Scoil Gharbháin, progression from the Naíonra to the primary school is seamless and therefore the Naíonra is an important foundation and integral part of life on the Scoil Gharbháin campus. As the population of the town of Dún Garbháin, and in particular the area adjacent to the Naíonra, continues to grow, Croí na nÓg wishes to ensure that the facilities provided in the town of Dún Garbháin are sufficient to cater for the demand for Irish-language based education for pre-school children in the town. It also wishes to ensure that suitable facilities are available to cater for the demand for Irish-language based pre- and post-school services in the area. The latter is particularly important as a significant number of parents of primary school travel into Dún Garbháin on a daily basis for employment and are likely to avail of such services if they were available. Croí na nÓg have recently purchased lands immediately adjoining the Department of Education and Skills lands upon which Scoil Gharbháin is constructed and wish to ensure that the lands are utilised in the most efficient manner possible to meet the Irish-language based early education and pre/post school service demands of the area. Croí na nÓg wish to appoint a consultant to undertake a Strategic Assessment and Preliminary Business Case as envisaged in the Infrastructure Guidelines and the tender documents to improve the range of early-years educational and pre/post school services in the area.

title-proc.eng: Assessment of the Performance and Effectiveness of Farmer Cooperatives and Farmer Groups in the Cocoa Sectors of Ghana and Ivory Coast

description-proc.eng: The primary objective of this contract is to conduct a comprehensive, large-scale study on the current state and effectiveness of cocoa farmer cooperatives and farmer groups in Ghana and Côte d’Ivoire (incorporating but not limited to cooperative societies in Ghana and COOP CA and COOP simplifié in Côte d’Ivoire). This study will represent the first nationally representative analysis of cocoa cooperatives and farmer groups across the two countries. It will uniquely combine data collection at two levels: (1) the organizational governance and operational management of cooperatives and farmer groups, and (2) the individual farmer members, including their engagement, benefits, and challenges. By integrating insights from behavioural economics, collective action theory, organizational studies, and development economics, the study will adopt an interdisciplinary approach to evaluate how structural, managerial, and behavioural factors influence cooperative performance and farmer outcomes. The reason for purchasing this service is to generate actionable insights that enable stakeholders, including farmers, cooperatives, policymakers, and certification bodies, to enhance the effectiveness and sustainability of cocoa production systems in Ghana and Côte d’Ivoire. Specifically, the study aims to assess the readiness of cocoa cooperatives for ARS1000 certification, evaluate cooperative governance and member engagement, and investigate household-level investment strategies, including investments in sustainable agricultural practices or household assets. The ultimate goal is to identify critical barriers and opportunities to strengthen cooperative capacity, improve resource allocation, and reduce the financial and operational burdens of compliance with sustainability standards, thereby contributing to a more sustainable cocoa production system in the region.

This shall include the preparation of all technical studies, surveys, modelling, assessments, reports, designs and application documentation required to secure the necessary approvals and to progress the Project to a stage suitable for procurement and construction. The Framework Agreement may subsequently be utilised by the Contracting Authority to procure additional related services, including procurement support, construction-stage services, post-consent services and other specialist consultancy services associated with the delivery of the Project. The successful Applicant shall be required to develop a fully integrated and coordinated scheme that delivers flood protection, surface water management, active travel and public realm objectives within a single coherent design solution that is environmentally sensitive, climate resilient and appropriate to the strategic importance of the Clontarf waterfront. description-proc.fra: L'Institut de géochimie et de pétrologie de l'ETH Zurich souhaite remplacer son microscope électronique à balayage (MEB) analytique actuel par un nouvel appareil équipé d'une source à émission de champ, de détecteurs d'électrons secondaires (SE) et d'électrons rétrodiffusés (BSE) de haute performance, ainsi que d'un spectromètre à dispersion d'énergie (EDS) de pointe à grande surface (≥ 100 mm²). Parmi les options possibles, nous sommes intéressés par des offres incluant un détecteur de cathodoluminescence panchromatique et/ou monochromatique d'entrée de gamme. L'objectif principal de cet instrument sera de réaliser des analyses quantitatives précises et exactes par EDS, en s'appuyant sur un protocole de quantification rigoureux incluant l'utilisation de matériaux de référence et une correction de matrice complète (ZAF, phi-rho-z ou équivalent). L'instrument devra disposer d'une chambre de grande taille permettant d'accueillir simultanément au moins 3 lames minces pétrographiques et 6 supports circulaires en résine époxy (format 1 pouce). Il devra également être programmable afin de permettre l'exécution de séries d'analyses quantitatives EDS automatisées d'une durée supérieure à 24 heures. Pour plus de détails, voir le cahier des charges.
description-proc.deu: Das Institut für Geochemie und Petrologie der ETH Zürich beabsichtigt, sein bestehendes analytisches Rasterelektronenmikroskop (REM) durch ein neues System zu ersetzen. Dieses soll mit einer Feldemissionsquelle, SE- und leistungsstarken BSE-Detektoren sowie einem hochmodernen energiedispersiven Röntgenspektrometer (EDS) mit grossem Detektorbereich (≥ 100 mm²) ausgestattet sein. Wir sind zudem an Angeboten für einen panchromatischen und/oder einen monochromatischen Kathodolumineszenz-Detektor (Einstiegsmodell) interessiert. Hauptziel des Instruments ist die Durchführung präziser und genauer quantitativer EDS-Analysen unter Anwendung eines strengen Quantifizierungsprotokolls, das die Verwendung von Referenzmaterialien sowie eine vollständige Matrixkorrektur (ZAF, phi-rho-z oder gleichwertig) umfasst. Das Gerät muss über eine grosse Probenkammer verfügen, die Platz für mindestens drei petrographische Dünnschliffe und sechs in Epoxidharz eingebettete Rundproben (Durchmesser 1 Zoll) bietet. Zudem soll das System programmierbar sein, um automatisierte quantitative EDS-Analysereihen mit einer Laufzeit von mehr als 24 Stunden zu ermöglichen. Details siehe Pflichtenheft.
description-proc.eng: The Institute of Geochemistry and Petrology at ETH Zürich is seeking to upgrade its existing analytical scanning electron microscope (SEM) for a new SEM equipped with a field emission gun, secondary electrons detector (SE) and high-performance backscattered electron detectors (BSE), and a state-of-the-art large area (≥ 100 mm2) energy dispersive spectrometer (EDS). Among several options, we welcome offers for panchromatic and/or entry-level monochromatic cathodoluminescence detector. The main goal of this instrument will be to provide precise and accurate quantitative analyses by EDS using a rigorous quantification protocol that includes the use of reference materials and a full matrix correction (ZAF, phi-rho-z, or equivalent). The instrument should have a large chamber to allow a minimum of 3 petrographic thin sections and 6 one-inch epoxy round mounts. It should be programmable so that we run series of >24 hours of automated quantitative EDS analyses. For further details, please refer to the specifications.

The meeting is open to all tenderers, both those who currently provide BPA services and those who are considering creating such a tender. title-proc.eng: Met Éireann Public Web Services

description-proc.eng: Met Éireann provides 24/7/365 operational forecast and warning services to the public. These services are provided digitally through a web portal (met.ie) and native mobile apps for Android and iOS operating systems. There is also a web portal providing access to observations from private weather stations (wow.met.ie). Met Éireann will be looking to procure hosting, maintenance and support and development services for these applications.. We are looking to work with organisations who can: 1) Configure and maintain a hosting solution to meet our challenging technical needs. The system will be expected to provide high availability and georesilience across multiple regions with contingency and disaster recovery applications to ensure continuity of service. Any infrastructure solution will be expected to meet the highest security standards assessed by penetration testing. 2) Develop the web portals and mobile applications based on the requirements provided. The web portal and mobile apps provide the following key services to the public and stakeholders: a. Communication and dissemination of weather and marine warnings, plus weather and environmental advisories. b. Communication of weather, marine and tailored forecasts eg farming commentary c. Presentation of radar and satellite imagery d. Presentation of analysis charts and data from Met Éireann’s observations network e. Presentation of data from private weather stations (wow.met.ie) f. Dissemination of climate services g. Interactive access to climate datasets h. Access to education and outreach materials, including the Met Éireann podcast i. Access to Met Éireann publications j. Access to information on Met Éireann’s scientific activities k. General information on Met Éireann including news articles and vacancies l. Contact helpdesk for various support channels, for example digital queries, climate enquiries m. Access to data, either through web page download or hosting links accessed from data.gov.ie The bulk of these pages have Irish language equivalents in line with Met Éireann’s obligations under the Irish Language Act. All web and mobile applications are subject to accessibility standards, which are routinely tested using an automated scan provisioned by the National Disability Authority (NDA). The anticipated development projects over the contract term are likely to include some or all of the following, but this list is not exhaustive: • Modernisation of mobile application code • Improvements to Content Management System (CMS) capability to enhance usability for Met Éireann staff. • Set up an archive to reduce operational load • Extension of Product Services (shared server) • Consolidation of Data Services – including extended use of APIs • Failover / DR solutions and processes for critical components • Enhancements to the 10 day location based forecast (Meteogram) • Ongoing enhancement of existing functionality as specified by Met Éireann stakeholders The application components will be expected to meet security and accessibility standards with support for Irish language content and responsive design. There should also be the ability to track analytics for each system component, with dashboards, notifications and alarms for Met Éireann operational staff. 3) Support and maintain the infrastructure and applications. Maintenance will be expected to be an ongoing activity for the infrastructure and applications, ensuring that components are kept up to date and overall system health is sustained. Support for the infrastructure and essential applications will be provided on a 24/7/365 basis to ensure continuity of critical services to the public and stakeholders. Our services are subject to intense scrutiny not just from the general public and stakeholders, but also through traditional and social media, hence short support response times will be set to minimise any loss of service time. This is necessary to ensure that Met Éireann’s operational teams have visibility that any issue is being investigated. The support team will not be working in isolation, there should be a close, collaborative relationship with Met Éireann’s operational IT, third party application support and forecast office teams. Further, well defined processes for management of critical scenarios would be established, with easily deployed failover/contingency solutions if the underlying issue will require significant time to resolve. Some of these failover and contingency solutions are already partially available, and further enhancement is included in the proposed development activities presented earlier. Lower priority issues should still be acknowledged outside of business hours, with resolution provided during normal business hours. All of the applications mentioned above are fully public and freely accessible and so potential tenderers are encouraged to review the functionality while assessing a response.

title-proc.eng: Caribbean Electricity Integrator Facility

description-proc.eng: The Caribbean Electricity Integrator Facility (CEIF) will provide integrated technical, engineering and transaction-advisory support to advance priority electricity-integration investments in the Caribbean from analysis and project identification towards investment and tender readiness. The specific objective of the contract is to validate regional Caribbean electricity-interconnection options and prepare, through an integrator approach, a St Kitts and Nevis-anchored Northern Corridor package that can reach at least tender or contracting readiness where feasible, while developing a replicable mechanism for future Caribbean electricity-integration corridors. The initial focus will be on St Kitts and Nevis, including the interconnection between St Kitts and Nevis and the associated generation, grid and enabling infrastructure required to support a viable integrated electricity system. The assignment will also assess the potential extension of the Northern Corridor towards Antigua and Barbuda and other Northern Leeward receiving/readiness nodes, subject to technical, economic and commercial validation. The contractor will assess the relevant technical, economic, financial, legal, commercial, environmental, social, institutional and procurement dimensions and develop viable business, financing, risk-allocation and procurement structures for priority investments. The work will also support the development of a scale-up and replication mechanism for a wider pipeline of Caribbean electricity-integration investments. The direct beneficiaries and geographical focus will include Caribbean partner countries covered by the EU-Caribbean Cooperation Facility+ and, where relevant to the electricity-interconnection agenda, Caribbean Overseas Countries and Territories and French Outermost Regions, with the precise geographical scope of subsequent corridors to be determined through the analysis. The contractor will provide an engineering-anchored transaction advisory team, combining strong power-system, grid and submarine-interconnection capability with expertise in market and demand analysis, economics, financial structuring, legal and commercial design, procurement, environmental and social safeguards and stakeholder engagement.

The current simulator park consists of equipment from different generations, with parts of the system being from 2014-2015. This leads to challenges connected to compatibility, operation, maintenance and support. The county therefore needs a more comprehensive system with more favourable functionality, simple administration and better interaction between the systems at the two school places. The simulators shall be used in training within navigation, vessel manoeuvring, radio communication, interaction and situation comprehension. The system shall support both the continuation of existing courses and the development of new training offers, and it shall be able to be used in teaching several certificate courses as well as by external users. It is therefore important that the system provides realistic training possibilities, high educational value and good user friendliness for both pupils, teachers and instructors. The delivery shall include simulator stations for pupils and instructors, the necessary hardware and software, the accompanying licences, cabling, integration with relevant existing equipment and adapted furnishing. The delivery shall be complete and ready for use when taking over. The system shall facilitate realistic training in navigation, manoeuvring, GMDSS communication, interaction between vessels and exercises across disciplines. The simulators shall be able to be controlled together from the instructor station, support joint scenarios and give good possibilities for real time management, recording, documentation and evaluation of exercises. Flexibility is also wanted for future expansions and integrations, including an option for a fishing module. The assignment includes further training in use and operation, documentation, proposals for a room system and any infrastructure requirements, as well as a service and maintenance agreement with support and access to spare parts. The system shall contribute to safe and efficient operation over time, with emphasis on user friendliness, central administration, upgradability and interaction between the simulator installations at the two schools.

title-proc.eng: Technical services agreement

description-proc.eng: With the publication of the contract notices for the Aramis Project four partners: TotalEnergies EP, Shell, EBN and Gasunie, started the execution of a project for a CO₂ transport and storage service, being the Aramis CCS Project ("Project"). This transport and storage service project aims to contribute to the energy transition by providing CO₂ transport to storage capacity in order to help enable parties that seek emissions reduction by means of Carbon Capture and Storage (“CCS”) at scale. The Project, a public-private partnership between the state-owned corporations EBN and Gasunie, and the private companies TotalEnergies and Shell. The Project brought together each partner’s technical expertise, experience, and knowledge of CCS. In April 2025 Gasunie, EBN, TotalEnergies and Shell have outlined the next phase of the Project including a new structure for the project with Shell and TotalEnergies withdrawing from the partnership of the transportation side to focus on the storage side of the project, while EBN and Gasunie will continue with the Project. It is vital for the Project to maintain and ensure that the specific knowledge and CCS knowhow of TotalEnergies will remain available to the Project. As such TotalEnergies is willing to continue to provide its specific operational support to the integrated Aramis value chain. To facilitate this support EBN and Gasunie have awarded TotalEnergies a contract for project support by making use of the negotiated procedure without prior publication of a contract notice pursuant to article 2.32(1)(b)(2) of the Dutch Public Procurement Act (Aanbestedingswet). The absence of competition for technical reasons is based on the fact that the Project's specifications, requirements and provisions are based on TotalEnergies standards and templates. As such the unique knowledge and experience of TotalEnergies with the set-up of the Project and the specific knowledge of the technical, operational and commissioning specifications is needed to be able to complete the Project. Achieving an equivalent level of knowledge and experience with another party would entail a significant time and cost impact, which the Project implementation schedule does not allow for. Furthermore, the costs associated with bringing another party to a substantially comparable level of expertise and experience would not constitute an efficient use of public funds. Accordingly, no reasonable alternative or substitute exists.
